title: Initialization reaches the canonical start
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state machine with $k$ work tapes over a finite alphabet, and let $x$ be an input word. After exactly $2k+2$ steps, the single-tape simulator started on the symbol-wise encoded input is in the canonical configuration representing the initial configuration of $M$ on $x$: its zone consists of one block starting at coordinate $0$, and its work head is at coordinate $-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state machine over a finite alphabet
replaced:
Let $M$ be a machine with $k$ work tapes over a finite alphabet $\Gamma$ and let $x$ be
an input word. Running the single-tape simulator for exactly $2k+2$ transitions from its
initial configuration on the symbol-wise encoded input reaches the canonical
between-steps configuration representing the initial configuration of $M$ on $x$, with a
zone of one block at coordinate $0$ and work head at absolute cell $-1$.
